title: Fin de soirée  (End of the Evening)

segments.t: Late at night outside her apartment building, Gabriel walks Chantal to her entrance. After spending the evening together, the two share a hesitant and polite goodnight farewell. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Voilà, nous sommes arrivés devant chez toi.
Merci pour cette très belle soirée.
Bon, il est tard maintenant.
Le temps passe très vite avec toi.
Oui, j'ai passé un excellent moment.
Je dois y aller maintenant.
Tu as une longue journée demain?
Oui, j'ai beaucoup de travail à l'agence.
Alors tu dois bien te reposer.
Toi aussi, repose-toi bien.
Bonne nuit, Chantal.
Bonne nuit, Gabriel.
On s'appelle bientôt?
Oui, avec grand plaisir.
Je t'appelle demain après-midi.
D'accord, à demain, Gabriel.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Voilà, nous sommes arrivés devant chez toi.
'Here we are, we have arrived in front of your place.' Gabriel signals the end of the walk home. The particle 'here' marks arrival at a destination.
Merci pour cette très belle soirée.
'Thank you for this very lovely evening.' Chantal expresses polite appreciation. The feminine noun phrase 'this' praises the shared time.
Bon, il est tard maintenant.
'Well, it is late now.' Gabriel notices the late hour. The impersonal expression 'it' states the late time of night.
Le temps passe très vite avec toi.
'Time passes very quickly with you.' Gabriel pays a gentle compliment. The adverbial phrase 'very' emphasizes how fast time flew by.
Oui, j'ai passé un excellent moment.
'Yes, I had an excellent time.' Chantal confirms her enjoyment. The compound past 'have' describes a completed positive experience.
Je dois y aller maintenant.
'I must get going now.' Gabriel prepares to leave. The modal verb 'must' followed by the adverbial pronoun 'y' expresses impending departure.
Tu as une longue journée demain?
'Do you have a long day tomorrow?' Chantal inquires about his schedule. The adjective 'long' qualifies the upcoming workday.
Oui, j'ai beaucoup de travail à l'agence.
'Yes, I have a lot of work at the agency.' Gabriel explains his professional obligations. The noun 'agency' refers to ASK.
Alors tu dois bien te reposer.
'Then you must rest well.' Chantal offers considerate advice. The reflexive structure 'yourself' expresses getting rest.
Toi aussi, repose-toi bien.
'You too, rest well.' Gabriel returns the affectionate wish. The imperative 'rest yourself' directly bids someone to rest.
Bonne nuit, Chantal.
'Good night, Chantal.' Gabriel offers a formal bedtime farewell. The standard polite formula 'good' bids someone good night.
Bonne nuit, Gabriel.
'Good night, Gabriel.' Chantal replies in kind. The reciprocal greeting concludes their conversation outside her door.
On s'appelle bientôt?
'Shall we call each other soon?' Gabriel suggests a future contact. The pronominal verb 's'appeler' expresses mutual phoning.
Oui, avec grand plaisir.
'Yes, with great pleasure.' Chantal accepts with enthusiasm. The polite idiom 'with' confirms keen agreement.
Je t'appelle demain après-midi.
'I will call you tomorrow afternoon.' Gabriel sets a specific time frame. The time expression 'demain apres-midi' denotes the next day.
D'accord, à demain, Gabriel.

'Okay, see you tomorrow, Gabriel.' Chantal brings the parting to a close. The parting phrase 'a demain' anticipates their next conversation. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.

Bonne nuit, Chantal.
Bonne nuit, Gabriel.
On s'appelle bientôt?
Oui, avec grand plaisir.
Je t'appelle demain après-midi.
D'accord, à demain, Gabriel.
Outside her building, Gabriel and Chantal exchange polite farewells after an evening out. Agreeing to talk again soon, Gabriel heads home.
